title: Germ reparametrization on strict towers and descent to integral derived morphisms
statement:
Fix the finite-field coefficient datum [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$. All schemes below have $\ell$ invertible and use compatible small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\widehat R_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$. Use $D^b_c(T,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], completed pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and point sections $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For a geometric point $v:s\to T$ and $M\in D^b_c(T,R)$ put $J_v(M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lv^*M)$. Stalks and their representatives $[U,u,a]$ mean [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For a strict tower $T_\bullet$ of complexes with transitions $t_n$, write $H(T_\bullet)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_T:\prod_nT_n\to\prod_nT_n)[-1]$, $s_T((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1})$, with degree-$i$ coordinates $(b,a)\in\prod_nT_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nT_n^i$ and differential $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_T)a,da)$.

Let $T$ be such a scheme, $v:s\to T$, $M\in D^b_c(T,R)$ and $\alpha,\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(k)$. Set $\delta=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ and $\epsilon=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta)$. For any flat-term K-flat $P\to M$, put $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat R_T}(A_n)_T$ with actual quotient transitions. On the bounded-tower replacements, and hence on the localized original towers, the germ rule
$$R_{v,\alpha,n}:(P_n)_v\longrightarrow(P_n)_{v\delta},\qquad[U,u,x]\longmapsto[U,u\delta,x]$$
is a natural $A_n$-linear isomorphism. These maps form a strict $R$-module tower isomorphism with inverse $R_{v\delta,\alpha^{-1},\bullet}$. Its whole-cone map is
$$H(R_{v,\alpha,\bullet})(b,a)=((\prod_nR_{v,\alpha,n})b,(\prod_nR_{v,\alpha,n})a).$$
Both coordinates commute with differentials and coefficient transitions. It is natural for all chain maps of representatives and compatible with the canonical quotient-cone resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Under the isomorphisms $e_{u,P}$ of [lem-trf-bounded-quotient-stalk-realization], it therefore determines a resolution-independent natural $R$-linear isomorphism
$$r_{v,\alpha,M}=e_{v\delta,P}^{-1}H(R_{v,\alpha,\bullet})e_{v,P}:J_v(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{v\delta}(M).$$
This naturality is for every morphism in $D^b_c(T,R)$, including roofs. The transformations on chain models descend through localization and their descents preserve identity and composition; the formula is unchanged when an arrow in a roof is inverted.

The equalities
$$R_{v\delta,\beta,\bullet}R_{v,\alpha,\bullet}=R_{v,\beta\circ\alpha,\bullet},\qquad R_{v,1,\bullet}=1$$
hold as whole tower maps and on both cone coordinates. They descend to the same equalities for $r$, and to every finite succession, with empty succession the identity. Here $\delta\epsilon=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta\circ\alpha)$; no commutation of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is assumed. No Weil structure or endomorphism of $M$ is required.

proof.text: To test equality of two normalized descended natural maps, first identify their equal point endpoints and their heterogeneous strict tower maps. For each constructible object use essential surjectivity of the good-complex localization to select one good representative. Postcompose both components by its target realization isomorphism. Their prescribed equations now have identical right sides. Cancel the realization and use natural-transformation extensionality.

proof.text: For composition, Spec.map_comp identifies the two target points in the correct opposite order. The two r comparison equations combine by associativity into the equation for the composite strict tower map, since integralOperationsRoosMap and the derived quotient preserve composition. Compare with the equation for alpha.trans beta using the preceding cancellation argument and the strict opposite action law. For the identity, Spec.map_id identifies the target point with the source, and the identity natural map satisfies the normalization by the identity laws of Roos and the derived quotient. The same cancellation proves the identity law. Assemble the twelve required clauses with the unchanged witnesses R,e,r.

The delivered Step 6 restricted the K-flat localization equivalence of lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent to the preimage of D^b_c(T,R), justified only by 'equivalent localized objects lie in the same full subcategory', and then applied lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property to it. A restricted localization is not a localization in general, because zigzags can leave the subcategory, and no cited node supplies the fractions argument that makes it hold here. Repair in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/<item>.json: Step 6 now writes every D^b_c morphism as a roof inside the flat-term K-flat representatives, citing lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated (D(A) is the category of fractions at quasi-isomorphisms), lem-pc-kflat-resolution (makes the roof apex K-flat) and def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed (a full subcategory with isomorphism-invariant conditions). r is now defined objectwise by the stated formula. Step 7 proves naturality, independence of the representative and uniqueness by conjugating along roofs. Step 8 cancels the middle e on each object. proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses were updated: the two new cites were added and site-derived-tensor-descent and the localization universal property were removed. The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint fields are unchanged, and the delivery has no new nodes. Step 5: the homotopy K=(-hb,ha) recomputed, and the mixed term cancels. Step 8: the order delta epsilon = Spec(beta∘alpha) is correct with no commutation.
